messages.content: Hey, it's your Northline Care weekly check-in. How are things going this week — any readings, symptoms, or medication changes worth logging?
Honestly not great. Insurance just denied my test strips again and I'm almost completely out. Been going back and forth with them for two weeks.

That sounds genuinely exhausting and I'm sorry you're in the middle of it. I have to be straight with you though — insurance appeals and coverage denials are outside what I'm able to help with from here. I can't do anything on that end. How have your readings been this week, or has anything changed with your medications?
That's what I'm saying, my readings are all over because I can barely test. Yesterday morning it was 187 and I have no idea if that's typical or not because I can't check it regularly anymore.

Logging that reading of 187 from yesterday morning. I'm not able to interpret what that means for you — that's a clinical question — but erratic monitoring combined with an out-of-range number is exactly what our nurses need to know about. I'm flagging this for a nurse now. They're showing a median response time of about 31 hours right now.
Will the nurse be able to do anything about the test strip situation?

I honestly don't want to promise something I can't back up — the nurse follow-up is specifically about your readings and clinical picture, not the insurance side. The coverage piece is still something you'd need to work through with your insurer or a patient advocate. I'll set your next check-in for next week. Hang in there.

theme: insurance denied test strips or a claim question
